clue.text: Remains presentable after his work's done

definitions.text: Remains presentable after his work's done

blocks.note: surface reading: someone stays smart and tidy once the working day is over
setter's reading: remains are a corpse, made presentable by this person's preserving work

explanation.surface: A worker who still looks neat and smart at the end of a long day.
explanation.walkthrough: Remains looks like a verb meaning stays; it is a noun for a dead body, which an embalmer preserves for viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmer treats a corpse with preservatives so the body can be viewed decently at a funeral.

clue.text: Being playful on Sabbath - chance to intervene in punishments

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so one word is set inside the other
in a down clue one part sitting on another is placed above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: S is a standard abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: Someone playing about on the day of rest risks being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Friskiness is lively, frolicsome high spirits, so a noun phrase like being playful describes it closely.

clue.text: Love rival at party in Spanish city

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, a round letter
to rival is to compete with
a do is a party; at just places it next

explanation.surface: A romantic rival turns up at a party somewhere in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is the capital of Asturias in northern Spain, a straightforward geographical example.

clue.text: Upset celebrity's annoyed expression

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A famous person, put out by something, mutters crossly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats! is an exclamation of irritation or disappointment, an interjection voiced when vexed.

clue.text: Permit to wear extra small skirts

indicators.note: something worn is enclosed by the wearer, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: in cricket a bye is an extra, a run not scored off the bat

explanation.surface: Permission for a small extra to dress in skirts, as on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: Skirts is not clothing but a verb: to skirt something is to go round its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt and to bypass both mean to go around something rather than through it, avoiding it.

clue.text: When head boy's first to go

indicators.note: the opening letter is to go away, so it is dropped from the front

blocks.note: bonce is British slang for the head
B abbreviates boy, and its first letter is the one removed

explanation.surface: Asking when the head boy will be first to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Head boy reads as a school prefect; head is the slang word and boy's first is just its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Once can mean as soon as, introducing a time clause in the way that when does.

clue.text: Director stops not so civil guide

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so one letter sits inside the other word

explanation.surface: A film director halts a guide who is being impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudder is the blade that steers a boat or aircraft, so it guides the vessel's course.

clue.text: Right, not left, passing through Czech region

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter that follows from the word before

blocks.note: L abbreviates left, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Travelling through a part of the Czech Republic, keeping right rather than left.
explanation.walkthrough: Right and left look like directions on a road; right is the adjective meaning ethical.
explanation.definitionFit: Moravia is a historical region forming the eastern part of the Czech Republic, around Brno.

clue.text: Bryan quickly shelters US citizen

indicators.note: what is sheltered is held inside, here across the two names before it

blocks.note: the letters run across the join between the two words

explanation.surface: Bryan hurries to give refuge to an American.
explanation.walkthrough: Yanqui is the Spanish-American spelling of Yankee.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanqui is a Latin American term, often disparaging, for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Refuse admission to loud women screamers

indicators.note: loud asks for what is heard spoken rather than what is written

blocks.note: females are shes, said out loud

explanation.surface: A club bars noisy women who shriek.
explanation.walkthrough: Women are shes; spoken, that sounds like the end of the answer, spelt with a double E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a female spirit whose wailing at night foretells a death in the family.

clue.text: American aims to get compensation

explanation.surface: A US claimant's goal is to be paid damages.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to make up for a wrong, so amends means reparation for harm done.

clue.text: Five of us in room excluding female - foolishly such types will swallow anything

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out, so the letter for female is removed
acting foolishly means behaving without order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: F abbreviates female, removed from the previous word

explanation.surface: Five people crammed in a room with no woman present, foolishly eating whatever is put in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnivorous animals eat both plants and meat, so they will consume any kind of food offered.

clue.text: Pervasive atmosphere is nothing serious

explanation.surface: A general mood that feels anything but grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Is nothing serious reads as a reassurance; it is just two pieces joined.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour can mean a lingering aura or air about something, as in an odour of scandal.

clue.text: Voices speaking, they may be apparent

indicators.note: speaking signals that we want the sound of the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: first meaning: expresses an opinion publicly
heirs apparent are those certain to inherit

explanation.surface: Voices heard talking may be easy to detect.
explanation.walkthrough: Apparent here is the legal sense in heir apparent, not visible.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a view is to state it openly, so airs as a verb matches voices.

clue.text: Top cops keeping it up around compound

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top
to keep something is to hold it inside, so the outer pair hold the rest

blocks.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: Senior police officers are keeping something up somewhere around the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the chemical compound that gives vinegar its sour taste and smell.

clue.text: Labuschagne finally cheered off - Poms annoyed, "That's a liberty!"

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the name
being annoyed means riled and stirred up, so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: Marnus Labuschagne is an Australian Test cricketer
taken as written; Poms is Australian slang for the English

explanation.surface: An Australian batsman is applauded off while English fans complain about cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: Labuschagne bats for Australia; Poms is Australian slang for the English, so the surface is an Ashes scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Free speech is a civil liberty, the right to express opinions without censorship.

clue.text: Trans loo confused some birds

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Birds are bewildered by a gender-neutral toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ortolans are small European buntings, notorious as a French delicacy eaten whole.

clue.text: He'll co-operate as I am a bit twisted

blocks.note: first meaning: one who goes along with a request
second meaning, playful: read as more compli(cated), a comparative of a shortened word for tangled

explanation.surface: Someone admits a slightly warped mind while agreeing to help.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: the answer split as COMPLI-ER looks like a comparative, slightly more complicated, that is a bit twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A complier is a person who complies, obeying requests or rules, so he co-operates.

clue.text: Brief quotations from Reichstag speech

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Short extracts from an address in the German parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Tags are short familiar quotations or stock phrases, such as a Latin tag.

clue.text: Hello! Streaker maybe drops dead in road

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so a letter is lost

blocks.note: D abbreviates dead, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A greeting as a naked runner collapses in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad street or road, often lined with trees.

clue.text: After ploughing, occasionally raid that farmer's land

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters are kept
ploughing turns the soil over, so the letters are churned up

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Once the field is ploughed, someone sometimes raids a farmer's property.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer's land reads as one phrase; the 's is just is, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for solid ground, dry land as opposed to sea or air.

clue.text: Key points are originally right

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: The main points are basically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a set of solutions, as in an answer key printed with a puzzle or exam.

clue.text: Sneaky scoundrel women support

blocks.note: a stand that props up a painting

explanation.surface: A shifty rogue whom women stand behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is figuratively a deceitful, untrustworthy person, from the animal's reputation for slyness.

clue.text: Troy kicked out of lodges in States

indicators.note: being kicked out means ejected, so a letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: lodges means stays as a guest
t abbreviates troy, as in the weight oz t, and is removed

explanation.surface: Someone called Troy is evicted from lodgings in America.
explanation.walkthrough: States looks like the USA; it is a verb meaning declares.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to declare it in words, which is just what someone does who says it.

clue.text: PM with Dutch national

blocks.note: D abbreviates Dutch; with just adds it

explanation.surface: A prime minister alongside Dutch and Israeli citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli was twice British Prime Minister in Victorian times.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli led Britain's government as Conservative premier in 1868 and from 1874 to 1880.

clue.text: Take exercise (and weed)

blocks.note: to do a class is to take it

explanation.surface: Advice to work out, with a sly aside about smoking cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope and weed are both slang names for cannabis.

clue.text: Series being shown featuring unknown US writer

indicators.note: a show featuring someone has them in it, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: a run of something is a series
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: A TV series being broadcast stars an obscure American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon was an American journalist and short-story writer whose tales inspired Guys and Dolls.

clue.text: About to leave purple with anger - that's silly!

indicators.note: something told to leave departs, so its letter is taken out

blocks.note: c for circa, the letter removed
to rile is to anger; with just adds it

explanation.surface: Someone turns purple with rage and storms out over something foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Purple with anger reads as one phrase about a red face; purple is the colour word and anger the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerile means childishly foolish, behaving like a boy, so it describes silly conduct.
